SYNTHETIC-SOLID-02: compact public Service demanded-decode regression fixture.
Generated input, generator and data: LICENSE.generated (BSD-2-Clause).
The test-only LZMA2 observer adapter mirrors sevenzip's BSD-3-Clause adapter;
its original copyright and permission notice are in LICENSE.sevenzip.
No archiver/codec executable is distributed with these fixtures.

Tool: 7-Zip 25.01 x64, 2025-08-03 (Debian package 25.01+dfsg-1~deb13u2).
Official primary source: https://www.7-zip.org/download.html
Tool executable SHA256:
60fc00b4e1ed37668972c51f03426973d8006db3c7224075878f6d66196d7c27
Generation (choose a new output directory):
python3 internal/mountfs/testdata/solid7z/generate.py --sevenzip 7z --out <OUTPUT>
Archive command:
7z a -t7z -m0=LZMA2 -mx=1 -md=1m -ms=on -mmt=1 -mhc=off -mtm=off -mtc=off -mta=off inner.7z member-a.bin member-b.bin member-c.bin
Fixed environment TZ=UTC, LC_ALL=C; inputs mode 0644. File times are excluded.
Two generations produced the same archive bytes/hash. Independent CLI `7z x
-so ARCHIVE MEMBER` matched every generated member before observation.

Payload algorithm: xorshift32 with shifts 13/17/5 using uint32 arithmetic.
Seeds 4100, 4101, 4102 respectively; take 16384 low bytes after each update and
repeat that nonzero/nonuniform block to exactly 4194317 bytes per member.
Go independently generates each expected member and checks its fixed hash.
Member SHA256:
member-a.bin eacaba81605ceb1a05168bbc3b5b7776afbaa6a2ca356a7a7a74e2852b8e816b
member-b.bin f3b67116ecaa30a554d6a58c52c9defbf6eda9588a0dad2230eab19af66a06d7
member-c.bin 2281935fa2a58077ef8f1fc83d468318eb01be4409946cac3694d80e24f61f68
inner.7z: 51981 bytes, SHA256
08b38858bb256efc500eda012e60887e6d852a122b6a04457d39e2ba1400f978
Layout: one solid plain LZMA2 stream, dictionary 1 MiB, 12582951 output bytes;
member offsets 0 / 4194317 / 8388634. Headers are not compressed (-mhc=off).
The Go test wraps inner.7z in generated ZIP Store and Deflate containers and
uses a local immutable HTTP Range source plus public Service APIs. No cloud,
FUSE or user data are involved, and a normal test needs no installed 7z tool.

This compact fixture has DIFFERENT plaintext and compression ratio from the
earlier issue #55 controlled baseline fixture. Layout/member sizes match, but
do not compare its HTTP bytes, compressed-input bytes or elapsed time as if
it were the same source. All metrics below were actually measured on this
new compact fixture at commit 52c8fe2, not copied from the earlier report.

Observation boundary: existing public sevenzip.RegisterDecompressor(method
0x21). A dedicated child test process registers a real LZMA2 factory mirroring
the pinned default constructor/config/Read errors/Close semantics, backed by
the same github.com/ulikunitz/xz v0.5.15 implementation. No production hook,
module replacement, pool implementation or uncommitted metadata API is used.
The existing pinned xz dependency is promoted from indirect to direct solely
because this test imports its real constructor; its version is unchanged.
The child isolation prevents process-global registration affecting other
tests; no private default-factory getter or unsafe restoration is needed.
Adapter reference: github.com/bodgit/sevenzip/internal/lzma2/reader.go as pinned
by github.com/binghezhouke/sevenzip 25c5d99319f0.

Count successful decoder construction and actual n returned by codec Read.
For the fixture's one plain LZMA2 coder, this is the group-output boundary.
These bytes include discarded member prefixes and requested member blocks,
not internal codec lookahead or CPU time. No wall-clock performance threshold
is used. Metadata/index seeding must initialize zero body decoders. Pool
residency facts for arbitrary registered decoders are not validated by this
test: the observer deliberately preserves the builtin codec parameters and
semantics. An admission rule refusing all registry overrides would require
a separate builtin observation seam, rather than relaxed custom-codec bounds.

All A/B/C public handles are opened simultaneously and remain live throughout
cold A/B/C head reads and warm C/B/A head reads (64 KiB each). Every returned
byte matches independently generated plaintext. Cache is 16 MiB, max depth 2,
max decode builds 1, read-ahead and streamed member fills disabled.

Measured RED at 52c8fe2:
cold A/B/C: successful decoder initializations 3; returned output 15728679.
warm C/B/A: additional initializations 0; additional returned output 0.
Required behavior: cold phase shares one forward decoder and returns <=10 MiB,
without filling the unrelated final member suffix; warm phase adds no decode.
This prevents an unconditional full-group fill (12582951 output bytes) from
passing as demand-preserving reuse. A 1 MiB demanded block per head yields
the forward group endpoint 9437210; the assertion tolerates up to 10 MiB.

Run from mount123:
go test -count=1 -run '^TestServiceNestedSolid7zSequentialHeadsShareDemandedDecode$' -v ./internal/mountfs
The performance assertions intentionally fail on 52c8fe2. With the shared
cursor, Store and Deflate ancestors both initialize one decoder and return
9437210 bytes; warm reversed heads remain 0/0. A tiny resident budget confirms
fallback returns the same bytes with the original 3/15728679 cost. An uncached
backward range followed by a forward miss adds only the one private backward
decoder; the shared cursor survives. Each read uses and then cancels its own
request context.

SYNTHETIC-MIXED-CRC-01 (issue #101): mixed-crc.7z
Generated by generate_mixed_crc.py using only Python standard-library code.
License: LICENSE.generated (BSD-2-Clause). Regenerate into a new destination:
python3 internal/mountfs/testdata/solid7z/generate_mixed_crc.py <OUTPUT>
Two Copy folders hold nine one-byte files with plaintext A through I. Folder
zero holds standalone.bin and declares its CRC; folder one holds member-01.bin
through member-08.bin, each with an explicit substream CRC. The eight-bit CRC
presence bitmap deliberately distinguishes compact digest count from file count.
7-Zip 25.01 independently reports Everything is Ok for the entire archive.
Size: 382; SHA256: 2063f178e602dab7cab604c0c64abc1898dd81342404a785379146c61950eba5
The Service regression wraps it in both Store and Deflate ZIP ancestors,
checks all nine payloads, and rejects a corrupted last member using its CRC.

Default single-file groups (#102)
--------------------------------
default-substreams.7z is an original 84-byte synthetic Copy archive generated by
generate_default_substreams.py (Python standard library only), under the existing
LICENSE.generated. It omits SubStreamsInfo and contains independent groups with
payloads A and BC. 7-Zip 25.01 accepts it; public Service tests cover a raw 7z
and Store/Deflate ZIP ancestry. There is no user or cloud content in the fixture.
SHA-256: 03248b13dc41a657ec5e40d997ee3fe66db4f5a830fe57c95a782e8bfea60e58

AES demand decoding (#55)
------------------------
encrypted.7z and mixed-encryption.7z use the same generated A/B/C plaintext
and LICENSE.generated. Regenerate into a new destination with generate.py
--variant encrypted or --variant mixed. Both keep clear uncompressed headers;
the public synthetic password is synthetic-solid-password. The encrypted
variant puts all three members in one AES→LZMA2 group. The mixed variant first
adds A without a password, then appends B/C with the password, producing a
clear group and an encrypted group. The generator independently extracts every
member with the 7-Zip CLI and compares it with its generated bytes.
AES IVs are random, so regenerated archive bytes differ while payloads and
layouts remain equivalent. Frozen fixture SHA256 values:
encrypted.7z d85b265debaf85bf53d5824eaa87ff1dfd3376cb9ca8c7988700a829c604b3a3
mixed-encryption.7z 5e207ef2f7210981933f4eb679bdb1e1bbf415a7e45ad0e97d62da0c6aeaa06f
The cross-adapter tests use a 64 MiB isolated cache and one build slot. Raw 7z,
ZIP Store and ZIP Deflate wrappers cover both plain and encrypted group reuse;
all cold heads initialize one decoder and return 9437210 bytes. Warm reverse
heads add zero decoder bytes. Budget fallbacks preserve plaintext correctness.
